name: Chronic Respiratory Distress with Surfactant Metabolism Deficiency

criteria.description: Persistent or progressive respiratory distress and hypoxemia in infancy or early childhood
Diffuse interstitial lung disease pattern on high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT)
Identification of pathogenic variants in surfactant metabolism genes (e.g., SFTPB, SFTPC, ABCA3)
Histopathological evidence of surfactant dysfunction with alveolar proteinosis or interstitial fibrosis
Exclusion of infectious, cardiac, or other known causes of chronic respiratory distress

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent respiratory distress with compatible HRCT findings and identification of pathogenic surfactant metabolism gene variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is critical for confirmation; lung biopsy may be reserved for unclear cases.

searchTerms: ongoing low oxygen breathing difficulty
chronic low oxygen respiratory distress
persistent trouble breathing with low oxygen

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse interstitial lung disease on imaging
searchTerms: widespread lung tissue scarring on scan
diffuse lung inflammation seen on imaging
interstitial lung changes throughout lungs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Failure to thrive secondary to chronic lung disease
searchTerms: poor growth due to chronic lung problems
failure to gain weight from lung disease
growth delay caused by lung illness

common.symptomName: Tachypnea at rest or with minimal exertion
searchTerms: fast breathing at rest or with little effort
rapid breathing without exercise
breathing quickly even when resting
bluish skin during feeding or activity
turning blue while eating or moving
cyanosis triggered by feeding or exercise
frequent lower lung infections
repeated bronchitis or pneumonia
enlarged fingertips and toes
clubbing of nails
bulbous finger and toe tips

laboratory: Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: High-resolution CT showing ground-glass opacities, interstitial thickening, and alveolar proteinosis
other: Lung biopsy demonstrating alveolar proteinosis and interstitial fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of genetic surfactant metabolism mutations
Rapid improvement with surfactant replacement therapy
May lack specific surfactant gene mutations
Variable age of onset and progression
